title: Granular retention combinator + evidence-synthesis playbook for request artifacts
creator: Ava Ramos
description: Problem: Customers need precise, auditable retention for prompts, responses, request logs, and aggregated metrics across mixed residency requirements (region, tenant, and legal holds). Existing work covers TTLs and per-route overrides but doesn't provide a single, deterministic mechanism that composes multiple signals (route policy, tenant residency, regulatory hold, adaptive sampling, and anomaly-driven preservation) into a final retention decision, nor does it generate compact, verifiable evidence snapshots for audits.
proposal: Introduce a Retention Combinator service that computes a canonical retention decision per request artifact by composing ranked signals: route-level TTL, tenant residency policy, active legal hold flags, anomaly-score retention triggers, and adaptive-sampling policies. Complement this with an Evidence Synthesis pipeline that can produce compact, redacted snapshots (sample + provenance + attestation) on-demand or on schedule. Key features: deterministic precedence rules, time-series tiering (hot/warm/archival), sampled-preserve windows for metrics & telemetry, per-region residency enforcement during export, and cryptographic attestation (hash chain + signed manifest) for each evidence bundle.
acceptance_criteria: Retention Combinator API returns a single retention TTL and disposition (keep, sample, redact, delete) for a given request artifact and context
Rules engine supports precedence: legal-hold > tenant-residency > route-override > anomaly-trigger > default-ttl
Evidence Synthesis can produce a signed bundle for a tenant containing N representative request artifacts with redaction rules applied
Exports respect region residency: data for EU-only tenants cannot be included in US-hosted evidence bundles
Console UI surfaces per-route composed TTL and a simulator that shows effective retention for sample requests
Integration tests that simulate overlapping signals (legal hold + short route TTL) and validate outcome
implementation_notes: Work broken into three milestones: 1) Rule model and combinator service (stateless API + policy DB), 2) Synthesis pipeline (Kafka -> worker -> signer) with redaction plugins and sample selectors, 3) Console + API for evidence exports and simulator. Use existing policy-store schema but extend to record precedence metadata and source-of-truth tags. Add a feature flag for toggling combinator evaluation in runtime path to allow gradual rollout.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Run combinator in dry-run mode to surface differences vs current TTL matrix and log mismatches. Phase 2: Enable per-tenant opt-in (beta) and run evidence synthesis for internal compliance audits only. Phase 3: Global opt-in and UI rollout plus automated scheduled evidence exports. Provide a rollback path by toggling runtime flag to fall back to legacy TTL decision path.
open_questions: What is the canonical format and minimum fields required in a signed evidence manifest?
How should sampled-preserve windows be sized for high-throughput tenants to balance cost and auditability?
Do we need tenant-level quotas for evidence export generation to prevent abuse?
Are there regulatory constraints for cross-border attestations that require separate manifests per-region?
risks: Cost increase from preserved samples for large tenants if sampling defaults are too generous
Complexity in precedence rules causing unexpected retention that could impact compliance
Signing key management for attestation requires HSM/KMS integration and rotation policies
metrics: % of requests with computed combinator decision vs legacy TTL (target 100% after rollout)
Average cost delta per 1M requests for preserved samples
Time to generate an evidence bundle (target < 10 minutes for medium bundle)
Accuracy of simulator (difference between simulated retention and actual after 24h)
Number of evidence exports per tenant per month
console_workflow: Add a Retention Debugger in Console: input a sample request, show stacked signals and final decision, allow preview of redacted evidence fragment and signed manifest. Add an "Evidence Export" page to request bundles and track export job status.
security_considerations: Evidence manifests must include hashes of included artifacts and be signed using customer or Redwood-managed keys depending on tenant preference. Redaction rules must be pluggable and vetted for PII. All export operations must be logged with auditor-level retention and require MFA for initiation in the UI for high-sensitivity tenants.
